speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) whether a comprehensive review of the outcomes of SkillsFuture will be undertaken before the next tranche of SkillsFuture credits is announced; and (b) if so, what will be the parameters of such a review.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: It is also about inculcating professional pride and greater depth of expertise in every field.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: As we move away from relentless pursuit of academic qualifications for their own sake, we are nurturing essential traits that will be future-proofing our people, such as curiosity to learn, resilience and entrepreneurial dare.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Most of all, the SkillsFuture initiative enhances our workers' employability, sharpens our industry competitiveness and opens up new opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: As our schools and higher education system move in this direction, we are also boosting the skills deepening initiatives, not just in industries, but also in our training institutions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: We are monitoring the progress and outcomes of all these initiatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: We are keeping a close watch on the scheme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As there was no timeline provided for when the next tranche of SkillsFuture Credits will be provided, could the Parliamentary Secretary further share when that is likely to take place?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Because if I look at the annual Budget Debate as well as the release, quite of lot, that is, $500 billion, is being set aside every year for productivity and SkillsFuture-related special transfers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The review is an ongoing process and I shared the four considerations earlier.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Ms Sun that many of the courses are highly subsidised by the Government to ensure affordability.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to better understand what is the area of training that is suited for their learning and development, with a view to strengthening Singaporeans' ownership of their lifelong learning journey.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: On behalf of the workers who have benefited immensely from the SkillsFuture Credit and also those who are constantly embracing lifelong learning, I urge the Ministry of Education to consider top-ups every three to five years.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I just want to reiterate my call and also the fact that this has benefited quite a number of people who have had to fork out from their pockets in terms of the unfunded portions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to just cite an example, the enhanced training support scheme for small and medium enterprises and the Workfare Training Support (WTS) scheme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we want to reassure Members that as long as Singaporeans are prepared to have a strong ownership of their lifelong learning journey and go for deepening of their skillsets, help will be available.
